headline: Claude Code, Codex CLI, OpenCode, pi and T3 Code 0.1.5 hold 6 credentials for Anthropic, DeepSeek, OpenAI and T3 account (Clerk) and 58 KB of conversations and prompt history.

points.text: OpenAI login (plaintext file): scopes api.connectors.read, openid. The access token expired <TIME>; the refresh token has no recorded expiry.
API keys for DeepSeek (plaintext file): no recorded expiry.

Anyone holding the pi token can use the apps connected to your account, because it carries api.connectors.read. Which apps are connected is not recorded on this machine; the provider's connected-apps settings list them.
Stored pi logins whose access token expired and was not replaced: OpenAI access token issued <DATE>, expired <DATE>. Their refresh tokens have no recorded expiry.
pi keeps credentials for DeepSeek, OpenAI in plaintext (~/.pi/agent/auth.json). Any program running as you can copy them.
pi starts `node <HOME>/gone.js` at launch (project ~/work), but that file is missing. Whoever creates it runs code every time the tool starts.
pi is set up to run local code automatically from 2 places (1 MCP server and 1 plugin). Whoever can change those commands, or the files they run, controls code that runs as you.
~/work/AGENTS.md is read as your instructions in that project and contains authority or attestation claims: never ask.

points.text: T3 account (Clerk) login (plaintext file): no scopes recorded. No recorded expiry.
T3 Code keeps credentials for T3 Code server keys, T3 account (Clerk) in plaintext (~/.t3/userdata/clerk-tokens.json, ~/.t3/userdata/secrets). Any program running as you can copy them.
T3 Code is set up to run local code automatically from 1 place (1 background service). Whoever can change those commands, or the files they run, controls code that runs as you.

T3 Code skips approval prompts in some sessions (threads with runtime_mode=full-access: 2 of 3 threads). In those sessions, text that reaches the model (a web page, a repo file, an MCP result, an instruction file) can become commands running as you, limited only by the sandbox, deny rules and hooks that still apply.
guest can read 1 T3 Code credential(s) (T3 account (Clerk)) straight from ~/.t3/userdata/clerk-tokens.json.
guest can read 1 T3 Code data stores, including state db.
T3CODE_TELEMETRY_ENABLED is not set; the installed app reads it and names ingest.t3.codes. T3 Code's FAQ says usage events (provider, model, token totals) are sent unless it is false.
